_comment: Per-fixture expectations for the round-trip gate (test/roundtrip.test.js).
Any corpus file NOT listed here must be editable and must round-trip byte-identically.
A file listed with identity:'fail' is a KNOWN defect. The gate asserts it still fails,
so fixing the parser forces an update here — that is the point. When a fix lands,
delete the entry and the file becomes a permanent regression test.
severity:'corruption' means the emitted file is not equivalent to the input —
it changes meaning or is invalid Astro. Those are bugs, not formatting drift.
severity:'formatting' means the output is semantically the same file, reformatted.

interleaved-frontmatter.astro.note: Imports are hoisted above frontmatter statements that originally preceded them. If a hoisted import's module has side effects, or a const is used in a later import path, hoisting changes evaluation order.

frontmatter-blank-lines.astro.note: Leading and trailing blank lines inside the frontmatter are lost to extraFrontmatter.trim() (astroParser.js:298).

four-space-indent.astro.note: serializeNode re-indents the whole tree at two spaces per level, so a project using four-space indentation has every page reformatted on first save.

copyright-as-authored.astro.note: A paragraph of text with an expression in it — `© {`${year} ${SITE_NAME}`}. All rights reserved.` — is written back on three lines, one per node. isInlineRun (astroParser.js) counts elements as inline but not expr nodes, so a run holding one is not recognised as a run and each child gets its own line. Renders the same (the breaks collapse to spaces); the diff is the problem.

full-page.astro.note:
Same cause as copyright-as-authored, in a page-sized file: `

We’re {SITE_NAME}, and we’ve shipped {stats.length} things since …

` becomes one line per node. Kept as a fixture because it also exercises entities, a map loop, a component, a style block and a script in the same file.

text-beside-block-element.astro.note: The hanging-bracket style — `<a href={href}` / `\t\t>Join our Discord <svg …` — is reflowed: tabs become the serializer's two-space indent and each tag gets its own line. The text's own boundary space survives the reflow now (that was the double-save bug); what is left is the indentation style, which the serializer does not preserve.

empty-frontmatter-dashes-in-body.astro.note: `---\n---\n--- these dashes are body text` — an empty fence followed by a body line that starts with dashes. The body's `---` is read as frontmatter code (model.extraFrontmatter === '---') and written back on a line of its own, splitting the sentence in two. Renders the same; the file is rewritten.

frontmatter-after-blank-line.astro.note: A blank line before the `---` fence, which Astro does not accept as frontmatter either — so the block is body text, and `const { href = "/" } = Astro.props;` parses as text, an expression and more text, landing on three lines. Astro renders both the same. The fixture is here because this is what a half-written file looks like mid-edit.
